correctness.rationale: For fixed strictly separated balls the indicator is the sum, and the real radial amplitude is r^(d/2) R^(-d/2) J_(d/2)(2πrR). Squaring its normalized asymptotic gives the stated weights and an O(R^-1) error; the off-diagonal term gets the extra O(R^(-(d-1)/2)) angular Bessel factor. For irrational ratio the time average of every nonconstant torus character tends to zero; compactness, tail recurrence and the vanishing error give both extrema and the continuous-test-function law. In rational ratio p:q the zeros and unit maxima have target phases (d+3)/4 and (d+1)/4 modulo 1 in the doubled phase convention. Eliminating the real phase gives qk−pℓ=(p−q) times the target, and coprimality makes integrality necessary and sufficient, including p=q=1. In d=3 and ratio 1:2 the normalized expression is z+4(2z−1)^2=16(z−15/32)^2+31/64, with maximum 5 on [0,1]. The companion code was inspected, not run; these are analytical checks, not formal verification.

originality.rationale: The headline lower-envelope claim is materially covered by a distinct indexed finding on all finite disjoint ball unions: that record states the same two-ball criterion, a stronger exact lower-envelope formula, and the same leading asymptotic. Its catalog date matches this record, so this is demonstrated coverage, not a finding about temporal priority or authorship. The upper criterion and explicit arcsine law are not stated in the inspected matching Finding; they are useful descriptions but routine consequences of that same expansion (phase complementation and standard continuous-time Weyl averaging), not a supported independently distinct surviving contribution on this evidence. No repair is proposed merely by deleting the covered clauses.
residual_risks: Same catalog date does not establish which finding was first; no chronology is claimed.
The literature inspection is statement-focused and does not certify historical priority or exclude older equivalent formulations.
